rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with an expanded Day 5 blastocyst and thinning zona, but it over-interprets single-image details by questioning the AA ICM/TE and mentioning debris/fragmentation that may not be reliably assessable.

Integrates age, AMH, oocyte yield, BMI, diagnosis, semen parameters, endometrium, and lifestyle well, with appropriate emphasis on diminished ovarian reserve affecting cumulative prognosis more than this embryo's immediate quality.

Reasoning is mostly logical and internally consistent, linking embryo quality and patient factors to prognosis; minor tension exists between calling the embryo good quality while repeatedly downplaying the lab's AA designation.

Recommendations are broadly consistent with IVF practice: SET for a good-quality Day 5 blastocyst at age 35, standard luteal support, caution with add-ons, and nuanced discussion of PGT-A. Minor deviations include speculative stimulation advice and some nonessential lifestyle restrictions.

Provides practical next steps for transfer and future planning, including SET, luteal support, prenatal vitamins, alcohol cessation, and when to consider further male-factor testing or PGT-A, though some future-cycle suggestions remain somewhat generic.
